failures: On /clients/hartwell-sons, Tab to the link 'edith@hartwelljoinery.example', Enter (and a mouse click): the page throws 'External navigation is not allowed' and nothing happens. Its href in the DOM is '/clients/hartwell-sons/mailto:edith@hartwelljoinery.example', not 'mailto:edith@hartwelljoinery.example': the router adapter's useHref treats it as a relative path and its navigate is called with it. It should be left to the browser as a mailto: link.

Enter on a list row (/ 'INV-1987, Hartwell & Sons Joinery'; /clients 'Hartwell & Sons Joinery'; a client's invoice row), at 1280 and 400: the address changes but document.activeElement is BODY on the new page; focus should be on main or its heading. Next Tab then starts from an arbitrary place (the skip link at 1280, the bottom navigation's 'Overview' at 400).
Enter on 'Go to Clients' (/reports) and on 'Go to Overview' (/nope/at/all): routed, but document.activeElement is BODY afterwards; same expectation.

The list rows are not links: each is a div role=row with data-href, no <a> and no link role inside (0 anchors in the grid), so nothing tells assistive technology that a row leads to a page and the browser's own link features are missing; the log's 'every link is a real <a>' is not true of them. unsure about the consequence I saw: a middle click on a row opened no tab in headless Chromium (Ctrl+click did).
could_not_exercise: Whether a mail client opens from the mailto link: headless Chromium has none; the thrown error and the wrong href are what was observed.
Space on a link or a row does nothing, as for any link; not counted.
